task: Close the post-#958 Control Plane release-unit execution gaps by binding the existing GitHub adapter to a least-privilege repository execution surface, implementing the canonical ALREADY_APPLIED no-code path, and automating final parent Completion Truth/Lifecycle consumption without creating a parallel release, proof or lifecycle authority.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: PR #958 merged the child Development Transaction binding and GitHub adapter, but the repository has no canonical workflow/job that invokes scripts/release-unit-execute.mjs in a real GitHub execution context. Static closure audit also proves that ALREADY_APPLIED is unconditionally converted to STALE/BLOCK despite the canonical no-code requirement, and that GitHub execution stops at PARENT_CLOSURE_ELIGIBLE instead of consuming the existing parent Completion Truth/Lifecycle path. A bounded production-like multi-unit rehearsal therefore cannot yet prove an operator-free end-to-end transaction.
observableOutcomes: A repository/GitHub execution surface invokes the existing release-unit adapter only for an explicit release-execution source namespace and uses job-scoped least-privilege write permissions instead of widening the ordinary CI token.

The execution surface consumes the canonical Plan Before Code release decomposition, persists/resumes the existing CAS execution state, and never recalculates manifest, Release Risk, Truth, Lifecycle or successor authority locally.

An ALREADY_APPLIED unit advances through an explicit no-code completion path only when every manifest operation is already applied at the exact current main and canonical exact-head proof obligations are satisfied; mixed or stale state remains fail closed.

After every release unit is CLOSED, the driver proves the final implementation main with the existing canonical gates, invokes the existing Completion Truth and lifecycle emitter, records the parent close receipt at that exact implementation main, and only then commits the closed parent plan through normal GitHub review/merge mechanics.
The source execution is interruption-resumable from the persisted state ref and stale/concurrent writers remain blocked by the existing force-with-lease CAS identity.

After this hardening merges, a separate bounded non-product fixture transaction can execute three or more release units through real GitHub PRs and merges without manual branch, receipt, successor, Truth or Lifecycle reconstruction.
unresolvedRisks: A write-capable Actions job could become a privilege escalation path if it runs on ordinary feature branches or accepts free-form scope, so trigger namespace, exact source identity and job permissions must be narrower than the normal CI surface.

Parent closure must be proven against the last implementation main SHA rather than the later plan-closure commit SHA, otherwise the existing recordReleaseParentClosure exact-main invariant would be weakened or misbound.

A source execution may be interrupted while child CI is pending or after a merge but before state persistence, so resume must reconcile only authoritative matching PR/merge/main identity and never infer success from timing.

The final parent proof must not fabricate gate outcomes; producer artifacts and exact-head workflow success must be consumed through existing verification semantics, with external proof applicability no wider than its producer trigger scope.

ALREADY_APPLIED can be safe only when all intended operations are already present and proof can bind to exact current main; a partially applied, renamed, generated or dependency-drifted unit must still block.

in: Bind the existing release-unit GitHub adapter to a narrowly triggered trusted default-branch workflow_run executor. The ordinary CI workflow only admits the dedicated source namespace; write authority exists only in the default-branch executor, which treats the source commit as data and runs trusted main executor code.

Add a thin bounded execution driver mode that initializes or resumes the existing CAS state, repeatedly invokes the existing adapter, waits only for authoritative exact-head child proof, and stops/fails closed on unsupported state or drift.
Implement the previously specified ALREADY_APPLIED no-code path inside the existing release-unit runtime/adapter without synthesizing a PR when exact current-main proof is sufficient.

Add a thin parent-close adapter that reuses existing Knowledge, Plan Before Code, Edit-Time, Incremental Replay, Release Risk, Quality/Type/Build evidence, Completion Truth, lifecycle emission and recordReleaseParentClosure semantics at the last merged implementation main.

Persist the canonical closed parent plan only after parent Truth/Lifecycle are verified at the final implementation main; the plan-closure commit may advance main afterward without changing the recorded implementation head.

Add adversarial regression coverage for trigger scope, permission scope, stale source/main/state ref, interruption/resume, ALREADY_APPLIED safe and unsafe states, parent early-close, final-main mismatch, closure-branch recursion and mutable receipt attacks.

Extend the existing Edit-Time Guard with a release-unit ALREADY_APPLIED evidence mode that validates the sealed materialization receipt against the exact child manifest/current main so Completion Truth receives canonical implementation evidence without inventing a parallel no-code gate.
out: No new Completion Truth, Lifecycle, Release Risk, Atlas, Sentinel, Knowledge, CI/CD platform or deployment authority.
No automatic product deployment, Vercel promotion, Supabase mutation, storefront, commerce, authentication, Builder or template behavior change.
No widening of Release Risk Budget, exact-head rules, Security Audit requirements, Sentinel requirements or external proof applicability.
No free-form workflow input may add files, change release-unit scope, replace Unit 2 manifests, reinterpret gate outcomes or choose an arbitrary merge target.
The actual three-plus-unit non-product rehearsal fixture is a post-merge proof transaction and is not predeclared as production implementation in this hardening change.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This code will hold GitHub write capability and can advance decomposed Development Transactions through real PR and merge state. The strongest practical deterministic assurance is required because a trigger, identity or closure mistake could merge unauthorized scope or falsely close a parent transaction; exhaustive bounded state/adversarial proof is appropriate while existing Release Risk and Completion Truth remain independently authoritative.

acceptanceCriteria: Only completed CI workflow runs whose event is push and whose head branch is under release-execution/source/** can enter the write-capable executor; the executor workflow is loaded from the default branch and checks out trusted main executor code rather than executing source-branch release scripts with its token.
The job cannot widen Unit 2 scope: source commit, target base, manifest digest, child binding digest, PR head/base and state-ref CAS identity are exact and fail closed.
A production execution can be resumed after interruption without an operator recreating branch, child plan, PR number, proof receipt, merge receipt or successor manifest.

ALREADY_APPLIED completes without a synthetic code PR only when all canonical operations are atomically already present at exact current main and child/parent proof obligations remain satisfiable there.
Any mixed already-applied/new content, target-base drift, stale generated identity, wrong proof task/head, mutable PR context or concurrent state writer blocks the transaction.
Parent Completion Truth and Lifecycle cannot run before every unit is CLOSED and can only close against the exact last merged implementation main SHA.
The closed parent plan is committed only after a VERIFIED parent truth and LEARN lifecycle candidate are produced by existing authorities; execution code does not calculate an alternate verdict.
A later bounded three-plus-unit fixture rehearsal can drive source→U1→proof→merge→fresh U2/U3→parent truth/lifecycle with no manual reconstruction.
invariants: Unit 2 release-unit manifest remains the exclusive execution-scope authority and neither workflow nor driver may add or reinterpret an operation.
Release Risk, exact-head child Completion Truth and existing lifecycle receipts remain authoritative producers; execution only validates and consumes them.
GitHub write permission is workflow/job-scoped on a default-branch workflow_run executor; source-branch workflow code and source-branch scripts never execute with the write-capable token.
CAS state persistence remains monotonic and a stale expected state commit can never be overwritten by a retry or second runner.
Parent closure evidence is bound to the final implementation main SHA recorded by the last CLOSED release unit, never to an arbitrary later main.
Security Audit, Sentinel and external proof applicability are not weakened by execution automation.

ALREADY_APPLIED implementation evidence is emitted only by the existing Edit-Time authority after exact manifest/receipt/main validation; the execution adapter may not fabricate GUARD-EDIT-TIME success.

failureModes: A write-capable runner starts outside the authorized branch namespace or with an unsealed source identity.
The runner resumes from stale CAS state and races another execution.
An ALREADY_APPLIED receipt hides a partial or semantically drifted unit.
Child CI is green but exact child Truth/Lifecycle artifacts are missing or foreign.
Main changes after a unit merge before successor reconciliation.
Parent Truth/Lifecycle are produced at a SHA other than the last merged implementation main.
Closure-plan persistence accidentally re-enters release execution or changes product scope.
edgeCases: The first unit is already applied at exact main and needs no code PR.
A later unit becomes already applied only after a predecessor merge.
The source workflow is cancelled while exact child CI is pending and a later run resumes from the state ref.
Squash merge produces a resulting main SHA different from verified child source HEAD.
Final implementation main passes CI while the subsequent closed-plan commit has a different SHA.
External Template Factory proof is not applicable to the execution-surface change and must not be fabricated.

alternatives.summary: Extend the existing CI workflow with a narrowly triggered release-execution job that calls the existing adapter and a thin existing-authority parent-close helper.
alternatives.reason: This reuses the repository's current GitHub/CI identity, existing Unit 2 manifests, release adapter, CAS state, Truth and Lifecycle while keeping write permission isolated to one explicit source namespace.

alternatives.summary: Keep the adapter command-line only and have an operator repeatedly run git/gh commands locally until every child PR and parent closure completes.
alternatives.reason: That would preserve the exact manual reconstruction and interruption-resume dependency the requested production-like rehearsal is intended to eliminate, and it would not prove repository/GitHub execution behavior.

alternatives.summary: Create a new standalone release workflow with its own risk checks, proof verdicts, state store and parent completion model.
alternatives.reason: That would duplicate canonical Release Risk, Completion Truth, Lifecycle and Unit 2 scope authority, violating the ecosystem rule that downstream execution must consume upstream machine-known facts.

specialistReviews.finding: The missing edge is an execution consumer and final closure binding around an already canonical adapter, not a missing release manager or Truth model.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep Unit 2 manifest, release-unit runtime, Completion Truth and lifecycle as owners; add only a thin CI execution surface and parent-close consumer.

specialistReviews.finding: A write-capable push job defined by the release source branch is insufficiently isolated: the same source commit could alter the workflow or executor script that receives GITHUB_TOKEN.
specialistReviews.resolution: Use a separate default-branch workflow_run executor with job-scoped contents/pull-requests/actions permissions. It checks out trusted main executor code, fetches the source commit only as data, re-runs trusted Plan Before Code/Release Risk projection against that source, and never executes source-branch release scripts with the write token.

specialistReviews.finding: The GitHub adapter already owns exact branch/PR/proof/merge and CAS semantics but has no repository job that drives it through pending CI and final parent closure.
specialistReviews.resolution: Drive the existing adapter monotonically, wait for authoritative exact-head receipts, and bind parent closure to the last merge receipt rather than reimplementing release decisions.

specialistReviews.finding: The closed #958 plan explicitly required a safe ALREADY_APPLIED no-code path, while current prepareActiveUnit converts every ALREADY_APPLIED receipt to STALE/BLOCK.
specialistReviews.resolution: Implement and adversarially prove the promised exact-current-main no-code transition, while preserving fail-closed behavior for partial, stale, generated or proof-incomplete states.

challenge.scenario: An ordinary feature branch modifies the release driver and receives a write-capable GITHUB_TOKEN.
challenge.finding: A broad token would let unrelated development scope create or merge repository PRs.
challenge.resolution: Keep top-level CI read-only and condition a job-level write token on the dedicated release-execution source namespace only.

challenge.scenario: Two workflow runs resume the same parent execution after an interruption and both try to advance the active unit.
challenge.finding: Without exact expected state-ref identity the active unit could fork or merge twice.
challenge.resolution: Reuse the existing force-with-lease CAS state ref on every persisted transition and fail the stale runner before any state advance.

challenge.scenario: A child PR exists but its CI is still pending, cancelled or green for a different head.
challenge.finding: Timing or generic workflow success cannot substitute for exact child Truth/Lifecycle evidence.
challenge.resolution: The bounded driver may poll, but advancement remains exclusively through importExactChildProof for the exact branch/head and matching child transaction artifacts.

challenge.scenario: Materialization reports ALREADY_APPLIED because all unit content is already present at exact current main.
challenge.finding: The current unconditional STALE/BLOCK implementation violates the canonical no-code requirement and would force a meaningless PR.
challenge.resolution: Add a dedicated no-code transition that validates complete already-applied operations and exact-main proof; any mixed or uncertain result still blocks.

challenge.scenario: One or more release units remain PLANNED, PR_OPEN, STALE or FAILED while a runner attempts parent closure.
challenge.finding: Automating final closure could accidentally collapse a partially completed parent transaction.
challenge.resolution: Parent-close code must require the existing closureEligible state, activeUnitId null and every declared unit CLOSED before invoking any parent proof.

challenge.scenario: The closed-plan commit advances main after the last implementation merge and parent truth is evaluated against that later commit.
challenge.finding: recordReleaseParentClosure requires the last unit merged main and would be semantically wrong if proof moved to the closure metadata commit.
challenge.resolution: Run parent Truth and lifecycle emission at the exact last implementation main first, record closure there, then persist the resulting closed plan in a separate normal closure commit.

challenge.scenario: Main advances between final-unit closure, parent proof and closed-plan persistence.
challenge.finding: A closure candidate could be based on stale implementation state or accidentally absorb unrelated changes.
challenge.resolution: Lease the final main to the last unit merge receipt throughout proof and closure-branch creation; any unexpected main drift blocks and requires fresh reconciliation.

challenge.scenario: The closure-plan branch also matches the source execution trigger and recursively starts another release execution.
challenge.finding: A metadata-only closure commit could accidentally initialize or resume a second parent driver.
challenge.resolution: Separate source and closure branch namespaces and allow the write-capable driver only on release-execution/source/** while ordinary CI verifies closure/**.

challenge.scenario: The driver sets final guard outcomes to success without corresponding exact-head producer artifacts or an authoritative workflow result.
challenge.finding: That would fabricate evidence and bypass Completion Truth proof semantics.
challenge.resolution: Rerun exact producer guards at final main, consume their artifacts through the existing verification checkpoint, and require exact-main CI success for Quality/Type/Build/Security before Truth.

challenge.scenario: A workflow input supplies a different source commit, target base or arbitrary extra file than the sealed Development Transaction.
challenge.finding: Free-form execution parameters would widen Unit 2 scope authority and make audit provenance mutable.
challenge.resolution: Derive source SHA from the workflow commit, base from origin/main and scope from Plan Before Code output only; do not expose file, base or merge-target inputs.

challenge.scenario: The driver marks GUARD-EDIT-TIME successful for an already-applied unit without running the canonical Edit-Time producer.
challenge.finding: Completion Truth could accept fabricated implementation completeness even though no child PR diff exists.
challenge.resolution: Add an explicit receipt-backed no-code mode to the existing Edit-Time Guard, validate all manifest operations as already applied at exact current main, and consume that producer artifact through normal verification checkpoint semantics.

challenge.scenario: A release-execution/source branch modifies its own workflow or release driver before a push and thereby controls code that receives contents:write and pull-requests:write.
challenge.finding: Branch-local job-level permissions alone do not establish a trustworthy execution boundary because workflow code is itself part of the untrusted source revision.
challenge.resolution: The write-capable executor is a separate workflow_run workflow loaded from default branch; it checks out main for executable tooling, fetches the source SHA only as a git data object, regenerates canonical decomposition with trusted main tooling, and rejects non-source workflow_run contexts.

proofPlan: Open a plan-only PR from the exact current main and require Plan Before Code PASS before editing CI, runtime or tests.

Prove the write-capable workflow is workflow_run/default-branch owned, rejects non-push and non-release-execution/source/** runs, checks out trusted main executor code, and never runs source-branch release scripts under its token.
Prove job-level permission isolation and branch namespace guards so normal CI stays contents:read and no pull_request event can enter release execution.
Add finite-state/adversarial tests for driver resume, stale CAS, pending/foreign child proof, merge/main drift and parent early-close rejection.
Add explicit ALREADY_APPLIED tests for all-applied exact-main PASS versus partial, stale, generated-identity or proof-incomplete BLOCK.

Run the existing Edit-Time Guard in sealed ALREADY_APPLIED mode and prove tampered receipt, partial operation coverage, wrong manifest/binding digest and wrong exact main all BLOCK before Completion Truth.

Prove parent closure consumes existing verification checkpoint, Completion Truth and lifecycle artifacts at the exact last implementation main and records recordReleaseParentClosure without a local verdict.
Run Edit-Time Guard, Incremental Replay, unchanged Release Risk, Quality Tests, TypeScript, Production Build and any canonically applicable external proof on the exact implementation head.
Require Completion Truth VERIFIED and Lifecycle Closure for this hardening transaction, merge it, and verify fresh main CI plus Template Factory applicability exactly as produced.
After merge, create a separate safe non-product fixture Development Transaction large enough for at least three release units and run it through the real release-execution source surface.
During the real rehearsal deliberately interrupt/resume once and exercise a stale CAS attempt without advancing authoritative state.
Do not declare the Release Unit Orchestration/Execution program end-to-end closed until U1→U2→U3+ and parent Truth/Lifecycle complete on real GitHub PR/merge receipts.

requirements.requirement: The repository exposes a bounded least-privilege GitHub execution surface that drives the existing release-unit adapter and CAS state without widening Unit 2 scope or ordinary CI write authority.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Ordinary feature, pull_request or main CI must not receive the write-capable release execution path.

requirements.requirement: Release execution continues to consume canonical Release Risk and manifest release scope and cannot convert a Release Risk BLOCK or scope mismatch into an executable unit.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: No execution-surface transition may reinterpret or bypass a canonical Release Risk BLOCK.

requirements.requirement: A fully ALREADY_APPLIED release unit can complete through an exact-current-main no-code path without a synthetic PR, while partial, stale or semantically uncertain application remains blocked.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Partially applied or stale unit state must never be promoted to completed no-code execution.

requirements.requirement: After and only after every release unit is CLOSED, final parent proof is produced by the existing exact-head verification, Completion Truth and Lifecycle authorities at the last implementation main and consumed by recordReleaseParentClosure.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Parent completion must not be recorded before all units close or against a SHA other than the final implementation main.

notes: Capability-closure audit after merged PR #958 found three concrete remaining edges before the promised production-like rehearsal: no GitHub workflow/job invokes scripts/release-unit-execute.mjs; prepareActiveUnit still turns every ALREADY_APPLIED result into STALE despite the canonical no-code requirement; and the GitHub execution CLI stops at PARENT_CLOSURE_ELIGIBLE without consuming the existing parent Truth/Lifecycle closure path. This transaction closes only those integration gaps. It does not pre-promote Knowledge and does not yet claim the overall Release Unit Orchestration program end-to-end complete; a separate real multi-unit fixture rehearsal is mandatory after merge. Plan-only PR #969 run 37518329190 correctly failed closed on projected-scope reconciliation. Canonical projection resolved the implementation to release-infrastructure / DOMAIN-RELEASE / release-infrastructure authority, active failure set SQ-KF-003/004/006/008/009/013/014/018/020/022 plus TF-KF-001/005/007/009/010/011/013/014/015, projected Release Risk 2/5, and guard digest 128614ad. The plan is reconciled to those upstream facts before any implementation edit. Pre-implementation state-machine audit proved the ALREADY_APPLIED no-code path cannot be implemented solely in the GitHub adapter because canonical verification currently requires PR_OPEN and canonical merge/close currently requires a PR-backed MERGED state. Scope therefore expands before the first implementation edit to scripts/lib/shoperation-release-unit-runtime.mjs plus its orchestration regression consumer; Plan Before Code must pass again before code changes. No-code proof analysis further showed that Completion Truth cannot accept a manually asserted implementation outcome when no child PR diff exists. The existing Edit-Time Guard must therefore gain a sealed materialization-receipt mode and remains the implementation-evidence producer. Scope expands to scripts/shoperation-edit-time-guard.mjs plus its regression consumer before implementation; no new guard ID or Truth authority is introduced. Plan-only PR #969 run 37519048754 narrowed the final projected subsystem to release-infrastructure while retaining DOMAIN-QUALITY + DOMAIN-RELEASE authorities, guard digest a41cfd0c, the broadened Known Failure set, and projected Release Risk 4/5. The plan is reconciled to that canonical projection before the first implementation edit. Pre-implementation security review found that a write-capable push job defined by the source branch would let that same source revision control token-bearing workflow/script code. The execution surface is therefore hardened before implementation to a separate default-branch workflow_run executor. .github/workflows/release-unit-execution.yml is added to canonical mustCreate scope; ordinary CI remains read-only and only provides the source-run trigger/admission context.
